messages:
alex.k: noticing a sharp increase in pod connection resets in eastus2 az4 since ~07:05 UTC. apps hitting object store and internal control-plane APIs failing intermittently. symptoms look like SNAT/conntrack exhaustion

sophia: are you seeing high conntrack_inuse? any prometheus alerts?

alex.k: prometheus alert fired: `ConntrackTableUtilization > 90%` on nodes in az4. infra-bot posted the alert earlier. quick dump from one box: `cat /proc/net/nf_conntrack | wc -l` => 960k (conntrack_max ~1M)

raj.p: logs show lots of short-lived outbound connections from pods with high source port churn. could be a client-side retry storm. also some 504s and TCP RSTs seen. handing over netstat/snmp output now.

infra-bot: [ALERT] conntrack_high on node gpu-eu-eastus2-az4-02 - 96% used. triggered at 1775001100.

alex.k: snippet of recent sysctl on the node:
```
# sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max
net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max = 1048576
# sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_count
net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_count = 962341
```

jen: any changes to MTU/overlay or RDMA? RDMA shouldn't touch SNAT but if kernel path changed it might.

taylor: we rolled an iptables/eBPF sidecar update yesterday on the GPU pools in az4, maybe that changed conntrack behavior. also saw an LB config flip that enabled proxy-protocol on 3 services.

raj.p: dumping conntrack sample entries shows many ESTABLISHED connections with random high source ports to 10.20.x.y:443 and ephemeral to external S3 endpoints. TTLs low -> churn.

alex.k: immediate mitigation options?
\
sophia: short term: increase nf_conntrack_max (sysctl) and bump conntrack hashsize if needed, and clamp conntrack timeout for CLOSE_WAIT/ESTABLISHED on our side to reclaim entries faster. also identify and rate-limit the offending pods.

raj.p: commands I ran on node to raise and evaluate (we should roll this carefully across nodes):
```
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=2000000
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_time_wait=30
cat /proc/net/nf_conntrack | wc -l
```

alex.k: increased to 2M on two nodes as a test. immediate drop in new RSTs but still high. need a cluster-wide fix.

taylor: longer term options: move to eBPF connection tracking bypass for outbound SNAT-heavy flows, or use per-node NAT gateway pods with conntrack tuning or keepalive reuse. also consider turning on source-port reuse / ephemeral port expansion.

jen: we should also validate ip_local_port_range on nodes. if it's small, ephemeral ports can be exhausted before conntrack.

raj.p: good call. current ip_local_port_range is 32768 61000 -> ~28232 ports. with many concurrent sockets and NAT mapping, that could be a bottleneck. recommended expand to 1024-65535 for busy workers.

sophia: action items: 1) infra to roll conntrack_max/hastsize increase + ip_local_port_range expansion to a pilot subset in az4 (taylor, raj), 2) app teams to surface retry loops and reduce churn (alex->ping owners), 3) monitoring: add alert for conntrack_count even if under threshold but with high churn rate / short timeouts (jen).

alex.k: I'll open a follow-up ticket and contact the largest traffic owners. For now scaling the conntrack table cluster-wide seems ok but we need to measure memory impact (conntrack uses kernel memory).

taylor: memory impact is the concern — double conntrack_max can increase kernel slab use. I'll run a memory-burst test on canary nodes. also will disable the iptables sidecar change on one rollout group to see if it reduces churn.

raj.p: also noticed NAT translations per node are spiking toward 128k for some nodes. we may want to add additional NAT gateway capacity or prefer SNAT-less routing for internal services in the VPC where possible.

sophia: documenting the temporary knobs and runbook: increase nf_conntrack_max, expand ip_local_port_range, reduce tcp TIME_WAIT, identify offender pods, consider eBPF bypass or per-node proxy. keep an eye on kernel memory and connection reuse metrics.

alex.k: ok started a CUE runbook and tagged owners. I'll post the runbook link here once done. thanks all, keeping this thread updated as we roll changes. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: incident log created: INC-2026-0421-cttable-flood-eastus2-az4
